Selection criteria of anchor pixels

Source: R/metric-anchors.R
ef_anchor_criteria.Rd

Gathers, in one explicit and auditable object, every criterion used by ef_select_anchors() to select the cold and hot anchor pixels of the METRIC calibration: the rules of each class, the homogeneity test, the final pick, the domain of the percentiles, the quantile type, and the source and verification status of the whole set. There are no default criteria (decision D-AP-01): the values used must be stated, with their source.

Usage

ef_anchor_criteria(
  cold,
  hot,
  homogeneity,
  select,
  percentile_domain,
  quantile_type,
  source,
  status
)

Arguments

cold, hot

Lists of ef_anchor_rule() objects (at least one each): the rules a cell must satisfy (all of them) to be a cold or a hot candidate.

homogeneity

An ef_homogeneity() object applied to the candidates of both classes, or NULL (no homogeneity test). Must be given explicitly.

select

A list with elements cold and hot, each an ef_anchor_pick() object.

percentile_domain

Character. Cells on which percentile thresholds are computed: "usable" (usable cells, i.e. allowed by qa and the search area, with no missing value in a variable used by the criteria) or "land" (usable cells with NDVI > 0, so that water does not shift the percentiles; the definition observed in water, CANDIDATA).

quantile_type

Integer in 1-9. Quantile type (Hyndman and Fan, 1996; the same definitions as stats::quantile()), used for percentile rules and the fraction picks. The result depends on it.

source

Character. Where the criteria come from (reference, preset or test parameters).

status

Character. Verification status of the criteria: "TODO", "CANDIDATA" or "VERIFICADA".

Value

A list of class earthflux_anchor_criteria with the arguments as elements.

Details

Invalid arguments raise errors of class earthflux_input_error (missing arguments: earthflux_missing_input; unknown choices: earthflux_unknown_method).

Verification status: no selection criterion is VERIFICADA. The automated procedures of Allen et al. (2013) and Morton et al. (2013) were only read in their abstracts; the criteria of the water package are a secondary source (dev/specs/anchor-pixels.md section 3). A criteria set labelled "CANDIDATA" must not become a silent default of the high-level interface.

References

Allen, R. G., Burnett, B., Kramber, W., Huntington, J., Kjaersgaard, J., Kilic, A., Kelly, C., & Trezza, R. (2013). Automated calibration of the METRIC-Landsat evapotranspiration process. Journal of the American Water Resources Association, 49(3), 563-576. doi:10.1111/jawr.12056

Morton, C. G., Huntington, J. L., Pohll, G. M., Allen, R. G., McGwire, K. C., & Bassett, S. D. (2013). Assessing calibration uncertainty and automation for estimating evapotranspiration from agricultural areas using METRIC. Journal of the American Water Resources Association, 49(3), 549-562. doi:10.1111/jawr.12054

See also

Other anchor pixel functions: ef_anchor_conditions(), ef_anchor_pick(), ef_anchor_rule(), ef_anchors(), ef_homogeneity(), ef_select_anchors()

Examples

# Test parameters that reproduce the defaults observed in the `water`
# package (CANDIDATA; not defaults of EarthFlux)
crit <- ef_anchor_criteria(
  cold = list(
    ef_anchor_rule("ndvi", ">=", 0.95, scale = "percentile"),
    ef_anchor_rule("lai", ">=", 4, scale = "absolute")
  ),
  hot = list(
    ef_anchor_rule("ndvi", "<=", 0.10, scale = "percentile"),
    ef_anchor_rule("ndvi", ">", 0, scale = "absolute"),
    ef_anchor_rule("albedo", "between", c(0.10, 0.35), scale = "absolute")
  ),
  homogeneity = ef_homogeneity("lst", window = 5, stat = "sd", max = 1.5,
                               window_na = "available"),
  select = list(cold = ef_anchor_pick("lst", "lowest_fraction", 0.2),
                hot = ef_anchor_pick("lst", "highest_fraction", 0.2)),
  percentile_domain = "land",
  quantile_type = 7,
  source = "water v1.0 anchors.control() defaults",
  status = "CANDIDATA"
)
crit
#> <earthflux_anchor_criteria> CANDIDATA - water v1.0 anchors.control() defaults 
#>   cold: ndvi >= p0.95 & lai >= 4; pick: lowest_fraction lst 0.2
#>   hot: ndvi <= p0.1 & ndvi > 0 & albedo between [0.10, 0.35]; pick: highest_fraction lst 0.2
#>   homogeneity: sd(lst) <= 1.5 in 5 x 5 window (available)
#>   percentile domain: land; quantile type: 7
